title: Ordinary localization from bifibrant homotopy recognition
statement: Use model categories, weak factorization systems, functorial factorizations, cofibrant and fibrant objects as defined in [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test], simplicial tensors and cotensors as defined in [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor], and the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Enlarge universes so the categories and localizations below exist as ordinary categories. Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category with a compatible simplicial enrichment, tensors and cotensors. Choose functorial trivial fibrations $QX\to X$ with cofibrant sources and functorial trivial cofibrations $X\to RX$ with fibrant targets. Let $\mathcal M^{cf}$ be its full subcategory of cofibrant fibrant objects. Suppose (i) a map between these objects is weak if and only if its vertex class in $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y)$ has a two-sided inverse, and (ii) for every fibrant $Y$ the two endpoint maps $Y^{\Delta^1}\to Y$ are trivial fibrations. Here $\pi_0$ is path components of geometric realization, equivalently vertex classes under finite zigzags of simplicial edges. Write $q:\mathcal M\to\mathcal L=\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$ for the ordinary category obtained from finite composable strings of ordinary arrows and formal inverses of weak equivalences, modulo the composition, identity and inverse relations. Let $H$ have objects $\mathcal M^{cf}$ and arrows $H(X,Y)=\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y)$, with composition induced by enrichment. Inclusion followed by $q$ descends to a functor $H\to\mathcal L$ and is an equivalence. An inverse sends $X$ to $RQX$ and an actual arrow $f$ to $[RQf]$. The comparison with the identity is induced by $X\leftarrow QX\to RQX$. For every arrow $a$ of $\mathcal M$, $q(a)$ is invertible if and only if $a\in W$. Every arrow in $\mathcal L$ between images of bifibrant objects is represented by an actual arrow between those objects.
